statusPage.title: System Status
statusPage.keeper_summary_default: Checks and runs pending matrix work
statusPage.keeper_info_note: The keeper runs checkUpkeep → performUpkeep on a schedule. When it detects pending work (parked rescues, force crosses, distributions), it submits a transaction automatically.
statusPage.parked_info_note: Parked members have cycled out of MatB but lacked enough withdrawable balance to re-enter T1 ($10). The Stability Fund contributes to rescue them. The keeper processes rescues automatically.
statusPage.matrix_info_note: MatA fills first (127 members), then force-crosses to MatB. When MatB fills to 127, the pool distributes and members cycle back to MatA. The keeper drives the crossing.
statusPage.sf_info_note: The Stability Fund receives 5% of every entry fee. It funds partial rescue contributions when parked members can't self-fund re-entry. A healthy SF > $200 can rescue 20+ members.

params.p1_hint: Cycles W1 must complete before auto-upgrade triggers.
params.p2_hint: Minimum cycles a wallet must complete before re-entering.
params.p4_hint: Time window for velocity checks (seconds). 3600 = 1 hour.
params.p5_hint: Minimum fills required within the velocity window to keep gate open.
params.p6_hint: Parked wallet % above which deflation mode activates.
params.p7_hint: Seconds before an idle slot is eligible for reclamation.
params.p8_hint: Max work items processed per keeper call.
params.p9_hint: Fee on withdrawals in BPS (150 = 1.5%). V8.21: targets a tier's PairManagerV8, which broadcasts the new fee to every MatA/MatB pair that tier has ever added (not just one matrix instance).
params.p11_hint: Duration of the voting window in seconds.
params.p12_hint: Delay between proposal passing and execution in seconds.
params.p13_hint: Minimum % of CNOVA supply that must vote (200 = 2%).
params.p14_hint: Maps each parked member's withdrawal ratio to how much StabilityFund coverage they get on rescue. Lower withdrawal ratio (less already claimed) → higher SF coverage.
params.p14_col1Hint: BPS of total earned already withdrawn. Row 1 is fixed at 10000/0 (full withdrawal = no rescue). Each row after must be strictly lower.
params.p14_col2Hint: BPS of the remaining shortfall StabilityFund covers at this threshold. Must strictly increase, capped at 10000 (100%).
params.p15_hint: Number of T5-first-entry members that activates the whale gate (extra anti-abuse check).
params.p16_hint: Days of inactivity before the days-based guard pauses a wallet. 0 disables this guard.
params.p17_hint: Cycles of inactivity before the cycles-based guard pauses a wallet. 0 disables this guard.
params.p18_hint: Master on/off switch for the inactivity guard (1 = enabled, 0 = disabled).
params.p19_hint: Seconds a parked member must wait before becoming eligible for rescue or eviction.
params.p20_hint: Withdrawal ratio (BPS of total earned) above which a parked member is evicted instead of rescued.
params.p21_hint: StabilityFund health target in USDC, used as a fallback. 100% of withdrawal fees route to the Buyback Reserve once balance reaches this. As of V8.21, the LIVE target usually auto-scales with the highest tier the system has organically opened (current tier entry fee x a per-tier multiplier) — this DAO-voted value only takes effect if that auto-scaling is switched off or not yet wired.
params.p22_hint: Share of SF inflow routed to CommunityWallet (BPS). 0 pauses routing without unsetting CommunityWallet.
params.p23_hint: Minimum SF balance reserved before any payouts. Capped at the current effective SF Target (auto-scaled or manual fallback) — can never exceed it.
params.p24_hint: USDC balance in the Buyback Reserve required to trigger a CNOVA buyback.
params.p25_hint: Maximum slippage allowed (BPS) on a buyback swap before it reverts.
params.p26_hint: Per-transaction whale cap on CNOVADirectSale, as a % of CNOVA total supply. 0 disables the cap.
params.p27_hint: Per-wallet whale cap on CNOVADirectSale, as a % of resulting CNOVA total supply. 0 disables the cap.
params.p28_hint: StabilityFund USDC target used to split each purchase's premium between SF and the liquidity reserve.
params.p29_hint: Liquidity reserve USDC target used to split each purchase's premium between SF and the liquidity reserve.
params.p30_hint: Final Frontier reward percentage paid out per epoch (range 10–75%).
params.p31_hint: CNOVA minted in an epoch that triggers the next halving epoch. Lower = faster halvings.
params.p32_hint: Unique members joined in an epoch that triggers the next halving epoch.
params.p33_hint: Maximum time an epoch can run before auto-advancing, even with zero activity.
params.p34_hint: Cliff vesting duration applied to future mints. Does not affect already-vesting batches.

params.p36_hint: Staking-duration boost lookup table — the longer CNOVA has been vesting, the higher the boost rate applied. Pass two empty arrays on-chain to disable; this UI requires at least one row.

compPage.page_subtitle: Every way CryptoNova pays you — from your first referral to a full matrix cycle at the apex tier. All logic lives on-chain. No admin. No gatekeeping.
compPage.card1_tagline: 10% of every entry fee paid straight to your wallet the moment someone you referred joins.
compPage.card2_tagline: 17% of every entry flows up 6 BFS levels. The deeper your downline grows, the more you earn automatically.
compPage.card3_tagline: 45% of entries accumulate in the equalization pool. When all 127 seats fill, the root member receives the full pool and auto re-enters.
compPage.card4_tagline: CNOVA tokens are minted to your wallet on every entry. Early epochs pay the highest rewards before halving kicks in.
compPage.card5_tagline: 10–19% of every entry fee flows into the CNOVA Treasury (rises at higher tiers). As more members join, the floor price only moves up — never down.
compPage.card6_tagline: Exclusive to the first 1,000 wallets ever to join. A dedicated pool, funded by a slice of every entry fee network-wide, pays out monthly — for life.
compPage.s1_p1: When someone joins using your referral link — or upgrades to a higher tier — your wallet receives a percentage of their entry fee instantly, on-chain, with no approval required. The rate is 10% at Tiers 1–3 and rises to 20% at Tier 4 and above. This relationship is locked permanently; every future upgrade they make keeps earning you the L1 bonus.
compPage.s1_p2_post: . If those 10 auto-upgrade through T2–T4, you earn the L1 bonus each time, from the same 10 people, again and again — at the higher 20% rate once they reach T4.
compPage.s2_p1: Every single registration in the network — regardless of who referred them — sends 17–20% of the entry fee upward through 6 BFS levels (the rate depends on tier). If someone joins anywhere below you in the matrix, you earn automatically based on how many BFS levels separate you. This is the passive engine of CryptoNova.
compPage.s2_p3: These payments are continuous — they fire every time a new member enters anywhere below you, not just at cycle completion. A deep downline generates chain pay from hundreds of entries passively.
compPage.s2_p4: At T5 ($250, 20% chain pay), the equivalent chain pay pool is $50.00 — so L1 earns $25.00 from each single entry below them at that tier.
compPage.s3_h3: accumulates in the equalization pool — paid on cycle
compPage.s3_p1: Every CryptoNova matrix holds 127 seats (a 7-level BFS tree). As each new member fills a seat, a share of their entry fee flows into that matrix's equalization pool — 44% at Tiers 1–3, stepping down to 26% at T4–T5, 24.5% at T6–T7, and 22.5% at T8–T10 (higher tiers shift more of the fee into referral and chain pay instead). When all 127 seats are filled, the member at position #1 (root) receives the full pool and is automatically re-entered into the next active matrix.
compPage.s3_p2: You don't need to be the root to benefit. Being earlier in the queue means more entries land below you, generating chain pay throughout the fill. Faster-filling matrices = more frequent earnings for everyone in the queue.
compPage.s3_p3: the protocol automatically re-enters the cycling member into the next active matrix. A portion of the cycle payout funds your re-entry fee — no manual action required.
compPage.s4_h3_pre: Minted to your wallet on every entry —
compPage.s4_p1: CryptoNova mints CNOVA tokens to your wallet automatically each time a new entry is registered (at any tier). The amount follows a halving schedule — similar to Bitcoin. Joining early captures the highest per-entry reward before each halving kicks in.
compPage.s4_p2_b: T1 Genesis epoch starting reward: 50 CNOVA per $10 entry.
compPage.s4_p2: From epoch 2, rewards halve cleanly every two epochs (40 → 20 → 10 → 5 → 2.5) before plateauing at 2.5 CNOVA. There are 9 epochs total — the last is the Final Frontier, formula-driven by the live floor price.
compPage.s4_p3_pre: Higher tiers mint more CNOVA per entry due to tier multipliers — a T10 entry mints
compPage.s4_p3_mid: the base epoch reward compared to T1. CNOVA total supply is capped at
compPage.s5_h3: of all entry fees back the CNOVA floor price
compPage.s5_p1_pre: 10% of every entry fee flows into the on-chain CNOVA Treasury. The floor price is calculated automatically:
compPage.s5_p2: The floor price can only rise as more members join — more USDC flowing into Treasury relative to new CNOVA minted means the backing per token increases. CNOVA holders can redeem for USDC at the floor price at any time, directly from the Dashboard, with no approval or lock-up.
compPage.s5_p3: CNOVA accrued during Genesis epoch at $0.02 floor could be worth significantly more at later epochs as the floor appreciates. There is no market-price ceiling — CNOVA can trade above floor on open markets.
compPage.s6_h3: Exclusive lifetime bonus for the first 1,000 wallets — paid monthly, for as long as you hold your spot
compPage.s6_p1: The 1% "Community Wallet" line in the entry-fee split below isn't just a protocol reserve sitting idle — every entry, from every member, at every tier, forever feeds this pool. What makes it special is who gets paid from it: only the first 1,000 wallets ever to register with CryptoNova are eligible to receive distributions, split into two permanent cohorts by join order.
compPage.s6_p2: Enrollment is automatic and permanent the moment you register — there's no separate sign-up, and it's capped at one slot per wallet address for life. Once the 1,000th member joins, the cohort is closed forever; no one can buy or earn their way into it after the fact.
compPage.s6_p3: every 30 days, anyone can trigger a distribution. Half of the pool's current balance pays out — 60% split evenly across all enrolled Genesis members, 40% split evenly across all enrolled Pioneer members. The other half rolls over, compounding the pool for next month. The pool is also topped up by orphan fees — entry fees that had no valid upline to pay and would otherwise be stuck.
compPage.s6_p4: Claim your share anytime from the Dashboard — unclaimed distributions expire after 30 days and roll back into the pool for the next round, so nothing is ever lost from the system, even if a member forgets to claim. Because the cohort is permanently capped, being one of the first 1,000 isn't just about earning chain pay sooner — it's a seat at a pool that never reopens, funded by every member who joins after you, for as long as the protocol runs.
compPage.table_footnote: Cycle payout = 127 seats × entry fee × pool share (44% at T1–T3, 26% at T4–T5, 24.5% at T6–T7, 22.5% at T8–T10). Chain pay L1 = entry fee × chain share (17% at T1–T3, 20% at T4–T5, 17.5% at T6–T10) × 50%. Direct referral = entry fee × 10% (T1–T3) or 20% (T4–T10). Velocity gates open when previous tier MatB reaches 80% fill.
compPage.table_footnote_b: Cycle payouts require the matrix to fill — not guaranteed.
compPage.split_h: 💰 Where Does the $10 Entry Fee Go?
compPage.split_intro: Every T1 entry fee is distributed automatically and instantly by the smart contract — no human intervention, no admin wallet:
compPage.split_footer_pre: 71% of every entry goes directly to participants (referral + chain pay + cycle pool). The remaining 29% builds the protocol — CNOVA floor backing, reserves, liquidity, and operations.

compPage.risk_body: CryptoNova Matrix is a high-risk DeFi protocol. Earnings depend entirely on continued network growth — if growth slows, matrix cycles slow and chain pay volume decreases. The cycle payouts shown above assume a fully-filled matrix, which is not guaranteed. CNOVA tokens are not a stablecoin and have no guaranteed market value above the floor price. Only participate with funds you can afford to lose entirely. This is not financial advice.

faqPage.page_subtitle: Common questions and term definitions for CryptoNova — bookmark this page for quick reference.

faqPage.g1_def: CryptoNova uses a 127-seat BFS (breadth-first) queue per tier — a 7-level binary tree. Members fill positions level-by-level. When all 127 seats are filled, the root member cycles out, receives their pool payout, and the matrix resets for the next cycle. Position determines chain pay depth.
faqPage.g2_def: The native reward token of the CryptoNova Matrix protocol. Minted and distributed to participants on each matrix entry. Has a rising floor price backed by the on-chain CNOVA Treasury. Not a stablecoin — market value can rise above the floor based on demand.
faqPage.g3_def: 10% of every entry fee flows into the on-chain CNOVA Treasury contract. The floor price = Treasury balance / CNOVA total supply. Token holders can redeem CNOVA at the floor price at any time — no admin approval required. The floor only rises as more members join.
faqPage.g14_def: 12% of every entry fee flows into the Stability Rescue Fund. It finances partial rescue contributions for “parked” members — those who completed a matrix cycle but didn't have enough withdrawable balance to self-fund re-entry. This is separate from the CNOVA Treasury, which backs the token's floor price.
faqPage.g4_def: 2% of each entry fee flows to the Dev wallet — it funds ongoing smart contract development, audits, and protocol engineering. It is not used for CNOVA redemption and is not accessible to individual members.
faqPage.g5_def: A stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the US Dollar, issued by Circle. The entry fee currency and payout currency for CryptoNova Matrix on the Base blockchain. Always carries 6 decimal places on-chain (1,000,000 = $1.00).
faqPage.g6_def: The smart contract that handles all member registrations. When you register, it determines your tier, routes your USDC to the correct matrix pool, mints CNOVA, and records your referrer permanently on-chain.
faqPage.g7_def: Each tier has two matrices (A and B). New members fill Matrix A first. When it completes (all 127 filled, root cycles), the system seamlessly switches to Matrix B so new joiners always have an active queue. The two matrices alternate, enabling continuous operation.
faqPage.g8_def: Financial systems that operate on blockchains without a central authority, bank, or intermediary. CryptoNova Matrix is a DeFi protocol — smart contracts execute all logic automatically, with no admin able to redirect funds.
faqPage.g9_def: The runtime environment that executes smart contract code. Base is EVM-compatible, meaning standard Ethereum wallets (MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, etc.) work seamlessly with CryptoNova Matrix.
faqPage.g10_def: A small fee paid in ETH to compensate validators for processing your transaction. On Base, gas fees are typically under $0.01 per transaction. Gas is separate from the USDC entry fee.
faqPage.g11_def: An epoch is a CNOVA distribution period. Each epoch starts with a set reward per entry. After a threshold of entries, the epoch advances and the reward decreases — similar to Bitcoin's halving. CryptoNova epoch names in order: Nebula Genesis, Mercury Rise, Lunar Cluster, Aurora Zenith, Solaris Echo, Cosmic Core, Galaxy Grid, Supernova Spark, Final Frontier.
faqPage.g12_def: The wallet that referred you when you first registered. Permanently locked on-chain and never changes — not even on tier upgrade. Your referrer earns the L1 referral bonus on your registration and on any tier upgrades you make.
faqPage.g13_def: The percentage of profit relative to the amount invested. In CryptoNova Matrix, ROI comes from chain pay (17% of entries flowing up 6 levels), referral bonuses ($1.00 per direct sign-up), equalization pool payouts ($4.40), and CNOVA token rewards. ROI is not guaranteed.
faqPage.q1_a1: CryptoNova Matrix is a decentralized, autonomous smart contract protocol deployed on the Base blockchain. It runs a 10-tier BFS (breadth-first search) matrix compensation structure where participants pay an entry fee in USDC and receive payments from subsequent participants according to predefined on-chain rules.
faqPage.q1_a2: CryptoNova uses a dual-matrix architecture (Matrix A + B per tier), a CNOVA Treasury that backs the CNOVA token floor price, and a unified smart contract entry point that handles all tiers seamlessly. The protocol is fully autonomous — no admin can pause, modify, or redirect funds.
faqPage.q2_a1: Connect a Web3 wallet (MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, etc.) on the Base network. Make sure you have USDC for the entry fee plus a small amount of ETH for gas (under $0.10).
faqPage.q2_a2: Go to the Register tab, enter a referral address (or leave blank for auto-assignment), approve USDC spending in Step 1, then click Join CryptoNova Matrix in Step 2. The smart contract handles everything instantly.
faqPage.q3: Do I need a referral to join?
faqPage.q3_a1: A referral address is required by the smart contract, but you can leave the field blank and the system will auto-assign you to a founding member. Anyone who joins through your personal referral link is recorded as your direct downline on-chain, permanently.
faqPage.q4: How much does it cost to join?
faqPage.q4_a1: Tier 1 (Nova Seed) entry fee is $10.00 USDC. Fees scale with each tier up to Tier 10 (SuperNova Apex). You also need a small amount of ETH for gas — typically under $0.10 on Base.
faqPage.q4_a2: Your $10 T1 entry is split instantly by the smart contract:
faqPage.q4_li1: $1.00 (10%) — L1 direct referral bonus to your sponsor
faqPage.q4_li2: $1.70 (17%) — Chain pay distributed across 6 upline BFS levels
faqPage.q4_li5: $1.20 (12%) — Stability Rescue Fund (funds rescues for parked members)
faqPage.q5_a1: Any EVM-compatible wallet works — MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, Trust Wallet, and Rabby are all supported. Make sure your wallet is connected to the Base network (chain ID 8453 for mainnet, 84532 for Sepolia testnet). Never share your seed phrase or private key with anyone.
faqPage.q6: What is the CryptoNova BFS Matrix?
faqPage.q6_a1: CryptoNova uses a 127-seat breadth-first search (BFS) matrix per tier — a 7-level binary tree. Members fill positions level-by-level: position 1 (root), then positions 2–3, then 4–7, then 8–15, and so on through level 7 (positions 64–127). When you join, you take the next available BFS slot.
faqPage.q6_a2: When all 127 seats are filled, the root member completes their cycle: they receive a payout from the equalization pool and re-enter at the next available position in the active matrix. The matrix then resets for the next wave.
faqPage.q7: What are Matrix A and Matrix B?
faqPage.q7_a1: Each tier in CryptoNova has two matrices (A and B) that work as a pair. New members always go into the currently active matrix. When it fills and cycles, the system switches to the other matrix so there is always a ready queue.
faqPage.q7_a2: The active matrix is shown on the Matrix tab. You can view your current position, which matrix you are in, and how many members are behind you.
faqPage.q8_a1: A cycle completes when all 127 positions in a matrix are filled. The member at position 1 (root) receives their equalization pool payout and is automatically re-entered into the active matrix at the next available slot. There is no manual action required.
faqPage.q8_a2: Throughout the cycle, chain pay flows to upline positions as each new member joins — earnings are continuous, not a single event at cycle completion.
faqPage.q9_a1: An epoch is a CNOVA mining period. Each epoch starts with a set CNOVA reward per entry. After a threshold number of entries, the epoch advances and the reward per entry is halved — similar to Bitcoin's halving mechanism. Early participants receive the highest CNOVA rewards.
faqPage.q9_a2: CryptoNova epoch names in order: Nebula Genesis, Mercury Rise, Lunar Cluster, Aurora Zenith, Solaris Echo, Cosmic Core, Galaxy Grid, Supernova Spark, Final Frontier. The current epoch is displayed on the Home and Dashboard tabs.
faqPage.q10: What is an upline and downline?
faqPage.q10_a1: Upline — members at shallower BFS positions than you in the matrix. They receive chain pay as new members (including you) fill positions below them.
faqPage.q10_a2: Downline — members who joined after you and are placed at deeper positions. Each entry they or their downlines make generates chain pay that flows up to you based on BFS depth.
faqPage.q10_a3: Your original referrer (the wallet that referred you) is a special permanent on-chain relationship separate from your BFS position — they earn L1 referral bonuses on everything you do.
faqPage.q11_a1: CryptoNova includes an auto-upgrade system. When you complete a cycle at your current tier, a portion of your equalization pool payout is automatically used to register you at the next tier up — no manual action needed. Your original referrer is preserved across all tier upgrades.
faqPage.q11_a2: Higher tiers have larger entry fees, larger chain pay amounts, and larger cycle payouts. You can also be upgraded manually from the Dashboard if you have sufficient earnings.
faqPage.q12: How do I earn with CryptoNova Matrix?
faqPage.q12_a1: Every $10 T1 entry generates income across four streams:
faqPage.q12_li1: Direct referral bonus — $1.00 (10%) — paid instantly to your direct sponsor. You earn this every time someone you referred joins or auto-upgrades.
faqPage.q12_li2: Chain pay — $1.70 total (17%) — distributed across 6 upline BFS positions as each new member fills a slot below you.
faqPage.q12_li3: Equalization pool — $4.40 (44%) — accumulates and pays out to the root member when a full cycle (127 fills) completes, then restarts.
faqPage.q12_li4: CNOVA tokens — minted and sent to your wallet on every new entry. Amount decreases each epoch (halving model). Starting at 50 CNOVA per $10 entry in Genesis epoch.
faqPage.q12_a2: The remaining split goes to protocol reserves and programs (CNOVA Treasury, Stability Rescue Fund, Dev, Ops, Liquidity Reserve, Buyback Reserve) — these back the protocol's long-term health and are not directly withdrawable by individual members. The exception is the Community Wallet: if you're one of the first 1,000 members to register, your share of that pool is claimable monthly from the Dashboard — see the Compensation Plan page for details.
faqPage.q13: How do I withdraw my earnings?
faqPage.q13_a1: USDC earnings (chain pay, referral bonuses, cycle payouts) accumulate in your on-chain balance. Go to the Dashboard tab and click Withdraw to Wallet. The smart contract sends your full withdrawable balance directly to your connected wallet in one transaction.
faqPage.q13_a2: CNOVA tokens are distributed directly to your wallet on every registration and do not require a separate withdrawal step. You can redeem CNOVA for USDC at the floor price using the Redeem CNOVA section on the Dashboard.
faqPage.q14_a1: No. Earnings depend on continued network participation. If growth slows, cycle completions slow down and chain pay volume decreases. Past results from any matrix structure do not guarantee future results.
faqPage.q14_a2: This is a high-risk protocol. Only participate with funds you can afford to lose entirely.
faqPage.q15_a1: No. All entry fees are processed directly by the smart contract and distributed instantly to upline wallets and protocol reserves. Blockchain transactions are irreversible. There are no refunds under any circumstances.
faqPage.q16_a1: When you first register, the wallet that referred you is recorded permanently on-chain as your original referrer and locked forever — it never changes, even across tier upgrades.
faqPage.q16_a2: Your referrer earns the $2.00 L1 referral bonus whenever you register at any tier. This rewards the person who brought you in for your lifetime participation.
faqPage.q17: How does the equalization pool and re-entry work?
faqPage.q17_a1: 44% of each entry fee ($4.40 at T1) flows into the equalization pool for that matrix. When all 127 seats are filled, the pool balance is paid to the root member and used to automatically re-enter them into the next active matrix — no action required on your part.
faqPage.q17_a2: If the pool accumulates before the matrix fills (from multiple cycles), the excess funds the root member's re-entry fee automatically. You can also top up your pool balance manually from the Dashboard if you want to accelerate re-entry.
faqPage.q18: What happens if I'm inactive for 90 days?
faqPage.q18_a1: If your account has had no on-chain activity for 90 days, the smart contract flags your position as paused. While paused:
faqPage.q18_li1: Chain pay to your position stops accumulating
faqPage.q18_li2: Your pool will not auto-trigger even if it reaches the re-entry threshold
faqPage.q18_li3: Your existing earnings balance is fully preserved — pausing never confiscates funds
faqPage.q18_a2: This protects matrix health — abandoned wallets do not block active members from earning.
faqPage.q19: How do I reactivate a paused account?
faqPage.q19_a1: Reactivation costs a small re-entry fee. Connect your wallet, go to the Dashboard, and click Reactivate. The contract will place you back into the current active matrix at the next available BFS slot, reset your 90-day activity clock, and resume chain pay to your position.
faqPage.q19_a2: All your previous USDC earnings and CNOVA are untouched — reactivation only re-enters you into the live matrix queue.
faqPage.q20_a1: CNOVA is the native reward token of CryptoNova Matrix. It is minted and distributed to participants each time a new member joins. It is not a stablecoin and not a security — it is an in-protocol utility token with a rising floor price mechanism.
faqPage.q20_a2: Starting CNOVA reward at Genesis epoch: 50 CNOVA per $10 entry. Starting from epoch 2, rewards halve every two epochs (40 → 20 → 10 → 5 → 2.5) before plateauing at 2.5 CNOVA. Total supply is capped at 21,000,000 CNOVA.
faqPage.q21: What is the floor price and how does it work?
faqPage.q21_a1: 10% of every entry fee ($1.00 per $10 at T1) flows into the on-chain CNOVA Treasury contract. The floor price is calculated automatically: floor = Treasury.totalBalance() / CNOVA.totalSupply().
faqPage.q21_a2: At launch with 50 CNOVA minted per $10 entry and $1.00 going to the CNOVA Treasury: $1.00 / 50 = $0.02 starting floor. The floor only rises as more members join and more USDC flows into the Treasury.
faqPage.q21_a3: You can redeem CNOVA for USDC at the exact floor price at any time using the Redeem CNOVA section on the Dashboard — no admin approval, fully on-chain.
faqPage.q22: How do I redeem CNOVA for USDC?
faqPage.q22_a1: Go to the Dashboard tab, find the Redeem CNOVA section, enter the amount you want to redeem, and follow the two-step process:
faqPage.q22_li1: Step 1: Approve CNOVA — allows the CNOVA Treasury contract to spend your tokens
faqPage.q22_li2: Step 2: Redeem for USDC — burns your CNOVA and sends USDC at the current floor price
faqPage.q22_a2: The USDC is sent directly to your wallet. The floor price shown is the live on-chain calculation at the moment of redemption.
faqPage.q23: How do I see CNOVA in my wallet?
faqPage.q23_a1: In MetaMask (or any EVM wallet), go to Import Token and paste the CNOVA contract address shown in the app footer. Once imported, your CNOVA balance will appear. The app also has an Add CNOVA to Wallet button on the Dashboard that does this automatically via MetaMask's wallet_watchAsset API.
faqPage.q24_a1: The CryptoNova contracts have undergone extensive internal testing including a comprehensive unit test suite and large-scale stress tests on Base Sepolia testnet. Source code is verified and publicly readable on BaseScan. Despite all efforts, smart contracts may still contain undiscovered bugs — participation always carries smart contract risk.
faqPage.q25: How can I verify the contracts on-chain?
faqPage.q25_a1_pre: All CryptoNova contracts are deployed and verifiable on
faqPage.q25_a1_post: . Search for the contract addresses shown in the app footer or Dashboard to read full source code and transaction history.
faqPage.q26: Can the team shut down or modify the protocol?
faqPage.q26_a1: No. The core matrix logic, fee splits, and reserve-fund mechanics are immutable once deployed. No party can alter entry fee distributions, redirect USDC, or access participant funds in the matrix contracts.
faqPage.q26_a2: The governance contract handles protocol-level settings and is subject to timelock delays and community approval. The team cannot unilaterally drain the Stability Rescue Fund or the CNOVA Treasury.
faqPage.q27: Which blockchain is CryptoNova Matrix on?
faqPage.q27_a1: CryptoNova is deployed on Base Sepolia testnet for community testing. Base is an Ethereum L2 built by Coinbase, offering fast, low-cost transactions (typically under $0.01). Mainnet launch on Base mainnet follows the successful completion of the testnet phase.
faqPage.q28: Is CryptoNova Matrix legal in my country?
faqPage.q28_a1: Laws governing cryptocurrency, DeFi, and compensation structures vary significantly by jurisdiction and are subject to change. The platform does not perform KYC or geo-blocking. It is entirely your responsibility to determine whether participation is legal in your country or region before joining. Consult a local legal advisor if unsure.
faqPage.q29: Do I need to pay taxes on my earnings?
faqPage.q29_a1: Tax obligations vary by country. In many jurisdictions, cryptocurrency earnings — including stablecoin payouts and token rewards — are taxable events. The CryptoNova protocol does not withhold or report taxes on your behalf. Consult a qualified tax professional in your jurisdiction.
faqPage.cta_p: Still have questions? Join the CryptoNova community on Telegram — we're happy to help.
